name: Kali Linux
description: Debian-based security distribution maintained by OffSec with hundreds of preinstalled tools.
purpose: Provides a ready-made testing platform for authorised work.
install: Download official ISO or prebuilt VM image from kali.org; verify SHA-256.
os: Runs in VMs on Windows/macOS/Linux; ARM builds available.
beginner: Start with the VM image, update with sudo apt update && sudo apt full-upgrade, take a snapshot.
interface: XFCE desktop; tools grouped in the applications menu; terminal is primary.
limitations: Not intended as a daily-driver OS
Tools need understanding, not just installation
detection: Defenders see Kali tools by their traffic patterns and user agents, not the OS itself.
ethics: Use only on systems you own or are explicitly authorised in writing to test. Unauthorised use can be a criminal offence (e.g. UK Computer Misuse Act 1990).
commands: sudo apt update && sudo apt full-upgrade

name: Parrot Security OS
description: Debian-based distro with security tools plus privacy tooling; lighter 'Home' edition available.
purpose: Alternative testing platform.
beginner: Use the Security edition in your lab VM.
mistakes: Same as Kali: running as root
ethics: Use only on systems you own or are explicitly authorised in writing to test. Unauthorised use can be a criminal offence (e.g. UK Computer Misuse Act 1990).

name: Ubuntu / Debian
description: General-purpose Linux distributions widely used on servers and desktops.
purpose: Target and server OS; stable base for tooling.
beginner: Install Ubuntu Server LTS as a practice target; harden it in Project 3.
limitations: Desktop not focused on security tooling
ethics: Normal admin use.

name: Windows (target and admin)
description: Microsoft's OS dominant on corporate desktops and AD servers.
purpose: Learn to administer, audit and harden Windows targets.
install: Microsoft offers free evaluation VMs/ISOs for Windows and Windows Server.
beginner: Build a small evaluation lab: one Windows Server DC and one client.
interface: GUI tools (MMC snap-ins), PowerShell, Event Viewer.
mistakes: Using Domain Admin for daily tasks
ethics: Use evaluation images legally.

name: Maltego
description: Graph-based OSINT and link analysis platform.
purpose: Visualise relationships between domains, IPs, people and organisations.
install: Download from maltego.com; Community Edition requires free registration with limits.
beginner: Start with a domain entity and run DNS transforms on a fictional or in-scope domain.
interface: Graph canvas, entity palette, transforms menu.
practice: Map silverline.test-style data in a lab
limitations: Some transforms need paid data sources
detection: Passive transforms usually do not touch the target.
ethics: Use only on systems you own or are explicitly authorised in writing to test. Unauthorised use can be a criminal offence (e.g. UK Computer Misuse Act 1990).

name: theHarvester
description: Gathers emails, names, subdomains and hosts from public sources.
purpose: Passive OSINT collection for authorised engagements.
install: Preinstalled on Kali; pip/git from GitHub.
beginner: Run against an in-scope domain with one public source and review results manually.
practice: Compare results against the supplied recon dataset
limitations: Results vary by source and API keys
ethics: Use only on systems you own or are explicitly authorised in writing to test. Unauthorised use can be a criminal offence (e.g. UK Computer Misuse Act 1990).

name: OWASP Amass
description: In-depth attack surface mapping and subdomain enumeration.
purpose: Discover subdomains passively and (with authorisation) actively.
beginner: Use passive mode first: amass enum -passive -d example.test.
interface: Command line with config file for data sources.
practice: Passive enumeration of a lab domain
mistakes: Running active brute force without approval
detection: Active brute force visible in DNS logs.
ethics: Use only on systems you own or are explicitly authorised in writing to test. Unauthorised use can be a criminal offence (e.g. UK Computer Misuse Act 1990).

name: Nmap
description: Network scanner for discovery, port scanning, service/OS detection and scripted checks.
purpose: Map hosts and services in authorised scope.
install: nmap.org; preinstalled on Kali; Zenmap GUI available.
beginner: Start with -sn discovery, then -sV on one lab host, and always save with -oA.
detection: IDS/IPS signatures, firewall logs showing many connection attempts.
ethics: Use only on systems you own or are explicitly authorised in writing to test. Unauthorised use can be a criminal offence (e.g. UK Computer Misuse Act 1990).

name: Wireshark
description: Packet capture and protocol analysis tool; tshark is its CLI.
purpose: Inspect traffic for troubleshooting, investigation and evidence.
beginner: Open a supplied PCAP, apply display filters like dns or http, use Statistics > Conversations.
interface: Packet list, details, bytes panes; filter bar.
limitations: Encrypted traffic is opaque without keys
detection: Promiscuous mode NICs can sometimes be detected; mostly passive.
ethics: Use only on systems you own or are explicitly authorised in writing to test. Unauthorised use can be a criminal offence (e.g. UK Computer Misuse Act 1990). Captures may contain personal data - handle under data protection rules.

name: Netcat
description: Utility for reading and writing raw TCP/UDP connections.
purpose: Banner grabbing, simple port checks, lab file transfer.
install: Preinstalled on most Linux; ncat from Nmap project for Windows.
beginner: Grab a banner: nc -nv <lab-ip> 21.
practice: Validate FTP banner in Scanning lab
ethics: Use only on systems you own or are explicitly authorised in writing to test. Unauthorised use can be a criminal offence (e.g. UK Computer Misuse Act 1990).

name: Burp Suite
description: Intercepting proxy and web testing platform by PortSwigger.
purpose: Inspect, modify and replay HTTP requests during web tests.
install: portswigger.net; Community Edition free; Professional paid.
beginner: Use the built-in Burp browser, set scope to the lab host, use Proxy history and Repeater.
interface: Tabs: Proxy, Target, Repeater, Intruder, Decoder, Comparer.
mistakes: Installing CA cert in daily browser
detection: Requests visible in web/WAF logs; active scanning is noisy.
ethics: Use only on systems you own or are explicitly authorised in writing to test. Unauthorised use can be a criminal offence (e.g. UK Computer Misuse Act 1990).

name: OWASP ZAP
description: Free, open-source web application security scanner and proxy.
purpose: Proxy, spider, passive and active scanning of authorised web apps.
beginner: Run a passive scan while browsing Juice Shop locally; review alerts and validate.
detection: Active scan traffic is noisy in logs.
ethics: Use only on systems you own or are explicitly authorised in writing to test. Unauthorised use can be a criminal offence (e.g. UK Computer Misuse Act 1990).

name: Nikto
description: Web server scanner checking for dangerous files, outdated software and misconfigurations.
purpose: Quick web server configuration checks.
beginner: Run against a local lab web server and validate each finding.
practice: Scan your own lab Apache server
mistakes: Treating output as findings without validation
ethics: Use only on systems you own or are explicitly authorised in writing to test. Unauthorised use can be a criminal offence (e.g. UK Computer Misuse Act 1990).

name: Browser Developer Tools
description: Built-in browser tools for DOM, network, storage and console.
purpose: Understand client-side behaviour and requests.
install: Built into Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari.
beginner: Open with F12 on a lab site; inspect Network and Application/Storage tabs.
practice: Inspect cookie flags on a lab app
ethics: Use only on systems you own or are explicitly authorised in writing to test. Unauthorised use can be a criminal offence (e.g. UK Computer Misuse Act 1990).

name: Postman / Bruno / Insomnia
description: API clients for crafting and organising HTTP requests.
purpose: Test APIs methodically by role and endpoint.
beginner: Import an OpenAPI spec and create collections per role.
mistakes: Storing real tokens in shared workspaces
ethics: Use only on systems you own or are explicitly authorised in writing to test. Unauthorised use can be a criminal offence (e.g. UK Computer Misuse Act 1990).

name: Nessus
description: Commercial vulnerability scanner by Tenable; Nessus Essentials is free for limited home use.
purpose: Automated vulnerability discovery with plugins.
beginner: Scan your own lab range with a basic network scan; then try a credentialed scan.
interface: Web UI with policies, scans and reports.
detection: Very visible in logs; IDS signatures.
ethics: Use only on systems you own or are explicitly authorised in writing to test. Unauthorised use can be a criminal offence (e.g. UK Computer Misuse Act 1990).
commands: (Web UI) New Scan -> Basic Network Scan

name: OpenVAS / Greenbone
description: Open-source vulnerability scanner (Greenbone Community Edition).
purpose: Free alternative for vulnerability scanning.
install: Greenbone Community containers; Kali package gvm.
beginner: Install via Docker/gvm-setup in a lab VM; scan your lab subnet.
limitations: Heavy resource use; feed syncs take time
ethics: Use only on systems you own or are explicitly authorised in writing to test. Unauthorised use can be a criminal offence (e.g. UK Computer Misuse Act 1990).

name: Nuclei
description: Fast template-based vulnerability scanner by ProjectDiscovery.
purpose: Run community templates for known issues and misconfigurations.
beginner: Run only safe/informational templates against lab hosts first.
practice: Scan local Juice Shop with tags
ethics: Use only on systems you own or are explicitly authorised in writing to test. Unauthorised use can be a criminal offence (e.g. UK Computer Misuse Act 1990).

name: John the Ripper
description: Password hash auditing tool supporting many formats.
purpose: Test password strength offline during authorised audits.
install: Kali package; openwall.com (Jumbo version on GitHub).
beginner: Practise on hashes you create yourself in your lab.
detection: Offline; detection focuses on how hashes were obtained.
ethics: Use only on systems you own or are explicitly authorised in writing to test. Unauthorised use can be a criminal offence (e.g. UK Computer Misuse Act 1990). Treat any recovered passwords as highly sensitive and never include them in reports.

name: Hashcat
description: GPU-accelerated password recovery/auditing tool.
purpose: Fast offline password strength testing in authorised audits.
beginner: Learn hash modes (-m) with hashes you generate in your lab.
ethics: Use only on systems you own or are explicitly authorised in writing to test. Unauthorised use can be a criminal offence (e.g. UK Computer Misuse Act 1990).

name: Hydra
description: Online login guessing tool for many protocols.
purpose: Test online password policies and lockouts in authorised, controlled tests.
beginner: Only against your own lab service with a tiny list - observe lockout and logs.
practice: Observe how fail2ban reacts in your lab
detection: Very visible: failed login bursts (4625, auth.log).
ethics: Use only on systems you own or are explicitly authorised in writing to test. Unauthorised use can be a criminal offence (e.g. UK Computer Misuse Act 1990).

name: Metasploit Framework
description: Open-source exploitation framework with exploit, auxiliary and post modules.
purpose: Controlled validation of vulnerabilities in authorised labs.
beginner: Use auxiliary scanners and 'check' commands against Metasploitable in your isolated lab.
practice: Read the Exploit Validation Safety lab first
limitations: Can crash services; detected by EDR
detection: EDR/AV signatures, network IDS, unusual services.
ethics: Use only on systems you own or are explicitly authorised in writing to test. Unauthorised use can be a criminal offence (e.g. UK Computer Misuse Act 1990).

name: Searchsploit
description: Offline search tool for the Exploit-DB archive.
purpose: Research public exploits for known vulnerabilities.
beginner: Search a software version, then READ the code before considering use in a lab.
limitations: Public code may be broken or malicious
ethics: Use only on systems you own or are explicitly authorised in writing to test. Unauthorised use can be a criminal offence (e.g. UK Computer Misuse Act 1990).

name: Aircrack-ng
description: Suite for Wi-Fi monitoring, capture and WPA/WPA2 passphrase strength testing.
purpose: Authorised wireless audits of your own networks.
beginner: Survey only your own AP with airodump-ng; test your own passphrase strength.
detection: WIDS detect deauth floods and monitor-mode activity patterns.
ethics: Use only on systems you own or are explicitly authorised in writing to test. Unauthorised use can be a criminal offence (e.g. UK Computer Misuse Act 1990). Radio interference may also breach telecoms law.

name: MobSF
description: Mobile Security Framework for automated static/dynamic analysis.
purpose: Analyse Android/iOS apps you are authorised to test.
beginner: Run in Docker and upload a deliberately insecure training APK.
ethics: Use only on systems you own or are explicitly authorised in writing to test. Unauthorised use can be a criminal offence (e.g. UK Computer Misuse Act 1990).

name: Android Debug Bridge (adb)
description: Command-line tool to communicate with Android devices and emulators.
purpose: Install test builds, read logs and inspect test devices.
install: Android SDK Platform Tools (free from Google).
beginner: Use with an emulator: adb devices, adb logcat.
practice: Check logcat of your own test app
mistakes: Leaving USB debugging on in daily use
ethics: Use only on systems you own or are explicitly authorised in writing to test. Unauthorised use can be a criminal offence (e.g. UK Computer Misuse Act 1990).

name: Practice Platforms
description: Legal training platforms: TryHackMe, Hack The Box, PortSwigger Web Security Academy, OWASP Juice Shop.
purpose: Authorised targets to practise skills.
install: Create free accounts; run Juice Shop locally with Docker.
os: Browser-based or VPN to platform labs; Juice Shop local.
beginner: Start with TryHackMe beginner paths, PortSwigger Academy for web, Juice Shop for local practice.
interface: Web dashboards, VPN configs, score boards.
limitations: Some content paid; platform rules apply
ethics: Follow each platform's terms of service.
